items.stem: According to paragraph 1, why is it a disadvantage for seeds to land directly under the parent plant?
items.sourceText:
Seed dispersal
Plants cannot walk, yet many species manage to spread their seeds far from the parent plant. This matters because seeds that fall directly beneath the parent must compete with it for light, water, and nutrients, and they are more easily found by animals that feed on seeds. Over time, plants have developed several strategies to move their seeds away.
Some plants rely on wind. Dandelion seeds, for example, are attached to light, feathery structures that act like tiny parachutes, allowing them to travel several kilometers on a breezy day. Other plants depend on water: the coconut's thick, air-filled husk lets it float across oceans and reach distant islands.
Animals provide another route. Many plants surround their seeds with sweet fruit. When birds or mammals eat the fruit, the seeds pass through their digestive systems unharmed and are deposited in a new location, often with a supply of natural fertilizer. Still other seeds have hooks that catch on animal fur and drop off later.
Each strategy involves a trade-off. Producing fruit costs the plant energy, while wind-dispersed seeds must be small and therefore carry limited food for the young plant.
options: They cannot be reached by the wind.
They must compete with the parent for resources.
items.explanation: must compete with it for light, water, and nutrients가 근거입니다. ④는 반대(동물에게 더 쉽게 발견됨).

items.stem: According to paragraph 1, why do cities cool down less at night?
items.sourceText:
Urban heat islands
On a summer afternoon, the center of a large city can be several degrees warmer than the surrounding countryside. Scientists call this effect an urban heat island. One main cause is the material that covers much of a city. Asphalt and concrete absorb sunlight during the day and release the stored heat slowly at night, so cities cool down less after sunset than rural areas do.
The shape of a city also plays a role. Tall buildings placed close together trap warm air and block the wind that might otherwise carry heat away. In addition, cars, air conditioners, and factories release heat directly into the air.
Heat islands are more than an inconvenience. Higher temperatures increase the demand for electricity as people run air conditioners, and they can be dangerous for elderly people and others who are sensitive to heat. To reduce the effect, some cities are painting roofs white so that they reflect more sunlight, while others are adding parks and green roofs, since plants cool the air as water evaporates from their leaves.
options: The wind is stronger at night.
Materials release heat stored during the day.
The countryside sends its heat to the city.
items.explanation: absorb sunlight during the day and release the stored heat slowly at night.

Hi Jordan,
I'm really sorry, but I damaged the book you lent me. Last night I was reading it at my desk and knocked over a glass of water, and several pages got wet. I dried them as well as I could, but some of them are still wrinkled. I know you need the book for your report, so I'd like to buy you a new copy this weekend. If you need it sooner, you can borrow my notes on the first three chapters until then. Again, I apologize for being careless.
Best,
Sam

items.stem:
Your university's student center plans to close at 7 p.m. instead of 10 p.m. starting next month. Write an email to the center's manager. In your email, do the following:
- Explain how the change affects you.
- Give a reason why the current hours are important.
- Propose a solution.
items.sampleAnswer:
Dear Ms. Lee,
I read the notice that the student center will close at 7 p.m. starting next month. I work part-time until 6 p.m. on weekdays, so the evening is the only time I can use the study rooms and printers. Many students who live off campus also depend on the center because the library's quiet floors are often full. Would it be possible to keep at least the study area open until 10 p.m., or to stay open late on the three days before exams? I would be happy to help collect student opinions if that would be useful.
Sincerely,
Jin Park
